record.category: WireGuard overlay with public TCP and UDP port forward

free_tier.stated: ProxyLink is currently free during early access, with no usage limits except a 200 MB recording cap; the published plan grid gives Free "3 proxy links (HTTP/HTTPS only)" and "No tunnels", and puts TCP and UDP behind the Developer plan at EUR 17/month

egress.terms: no usage limits except those noted below; the only noted limit is 'Recording storage is limited to 200 MB per account'; ingress: tcp+udp

record.interface_detail: 'import the .conf file in under 2 minutes'; the dashboard assigns the public port
record.tooling: any WireGuard client; browser dashboard; MikroTik one-click autoconfig
record.chaining: The only managed service found that issues a WG peer and forwards arbitrary TCP and UDP, and the free version of that path is time-limited: today everything is free, after early access the free plan is HTTP proxy links only
record.limits_note: The same vendor publishes a paid grid that gives Free zero tunnels: Free is "3 proxy links (HTTP/HTTPS only)", "No tunnels"; Developer is EUR 17/month and carries "5 tunnels"; MSP is EUR 69/month and carries 300. The TCP/UDP doc says "TCP links require an active tunnel (VPN)", and the pricing FAQ says "TCP links, browser SSH/RDP/VNC, and LAN access all require a tunnel (Developer plan or above)". So the free tier has no published TCP or UDP path once early access ends.
record.binding_note: No byte quota, no rate and no published consumption meter exist, so nothing in the vocabulary fails in bytes; what ends the arrangement is the end of early access, and the exit price is already published at EUR 17/month

identity_cost.detail: 'Early Access - everything free, no credit card.' and 'No card. No trial countdown.' The registration form at app.proxylink.dev/register was not read.

record.reliability_note: The free arrangement is bounded by the early-access period rather than by a quota; the vendor states the post-launch position in its own plan grid
record.confidence_note: A live UDP packet to tcp.proxylink.dev:PORT and back from a peer would raise this to measured.

evidence.proved: UDP and TCP tunnel links, the tcp.proxylink.dev host with a per-link port, and the UDP transparency sentence
'currently free during early access ... there are no usage limits except those noted below' and the 200 MB recording cap
.conf import, one WireGuard peer per account, and EU-only proxying on Hetzner Germany

Free plan: '3 proxy links (HTTP/HTTPS only)', 'No tunnels', 'No browser terminals', 'No custom domains'; Developer 'EUR 17 / month' with '5 tunnels'; FAQ: 'TCP links, browser SSH/RDP/VNC, and LAN access all require a tunnel (Developer plan or above)'

record.notes: An adversarial re-read on 2026-10-23 opened proxylink.dev/pricing, which this record had never read. It publishes a free plan with no tunnels at all, and the TCP and UDP docs say a TCP link requires an active tunnel. The early-access sentence is still true today and it is the whole of the free path. Verdict moved from qualifies-with-caveat to trial-only because the free arrangement has a published end and a published price.

extras.wg_detail: 'OpenWRT, pfSense, OPNsense, TP-Link - import the .conf file in under 2 minutes.' One peer covers the account: 'issue them one WireGuard peer for your whole account, not one per client site'.
extras.volume_stated: no usage limits except those noted below; the only noted limit is 'Recording storage is limited to 200 MB per account'
extras.transit_note: ProxyLink's proxy cluster in Hetzner Germany terminates the public side and relays over WireGuard to the peer
